title: Path Selector Degradation — Remediation and Validation Runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a stealth rollout of the path selector heuristic (aimed at reducing cost by preferring quantized kernels for short sequences), we observed a reproducible p95 latency regression on a subset of pinned models and routing configurations. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations, and a validation runbook to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: From 2026-02-27 03:00 to 2026-02-28 11:00 UTC we saw a 1.6x increase in p95 for interactive traces on redwood-small-1 in the hosted region eu-west-1. Customer-facing error rates remained <0.1%, but tail latency spikes caused degraded UX for several high-traffic customers and triggered paging for on-call.
timeline: 2026-02-27 02:30 UTC: Canary rollout of path-selector heuristic v0.9 begins targeting 10% of traffic (internal experiment).
2026-02-27 03:15 UTC: Dashboard alert: p95 for redwood-small-1 rises from baseline 120ms to ~200ms. Initial suspicion: batching changes.
2026-02-27 03:45 UTC: On-call team routes affected traffic to fallback runtime, p95 returns to baseline.
2026-02-27 06:00 UTC: Hotfix: rollout paused and config toggled to force previous kernel ranking. Immediate mitigation reduces incidents.
2026-02-27 09:30 UTC: Collected representative traces and saved KV-caches and batch profiles to s3://redwood-ops/incident/ENG-51321/ for root cause analysis.
2026-03-01 10:00 UTC: Formal ticket opened; larger investigation assigned to runtime-kernels squad.
root_cause: The path-selector heuristic incorrectly scored a quantized GEMM kernel higher than the fused attention kernel for short context lengths when micro-batch distribution produced mostly single-token steps. The scoring function underestimated fixed overheads for the quantized path (memory layout transforms + dequantize/quantize) causing higher end-to-end latency at p95 despite better average throughput.
decisions: Revert canary: keep path-selector disabled for public rollout until fixes are validated.
Add conservative guard: require a positive A/B p95 win before automatic preference of quantized kernels for any model architecture.
Introduce synthetic micro-batch regression tests into CI that exercise 1-token to 8-token patterns at scale.
Publish a performance contract for kernel swaps: candidate must show <=5% p95 regression across representative prompt sets and cost telemetry.
action_items: Migrate the path-selector scoring to include estimated transform overhead (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-03-10).
Add micro-batch synthetic benchmark to nightly CI and block merges that increase historical p95 by >7% (owner: Li Chen, due: 2026-03-15).
Extend Canary gating to include p95, regional percentiles, and representative customer keys (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-03-08).
Run retrospective with product and solutions teams to identify top 5 customers impacted and coordinate communications (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2026-03-05).
Backfill telemetry: surface kernel transition counts per model and per-route in Console for 90-day retention (owner: Observability Squad, due: 2026-04-01).
Create a rollback playbook that includes cache warmup steps and expected transient latency (owner: On-call Lead, due: 2026-03-07).
validation_plan: 1) Unit/regression tests: Add deterministic micro-batch cases (1..8 tokens) for each kernel candidate. 2) Bench: Run nightly against redwood-small-1 and redwood-medium-1 with representative prompt sets; assert p50 and p95 don't regress >5%. 3) Staged canary: start at 1% traffic, monitor p95 and kernel transition delta for 24h, then 5%, then 20% with explicit manual gate at each step. 4) Post-release: run 48h golden-run comparison vs baseline and verify SLA metrics.
